<awtsmoosMeluketTranslation heichel="ikar" alias="meluket_translation_en" seriesId="תמוז_meluket" postId="BH_POST_1766518919374_theRebbe_640" batchId="meluket-_D7_AA_D7_9E_D7_95_D7_96_meluket__BH_POST_1766518919374_theRebbe_640__p003">
  <section v="6">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section explains how the concept that prayer draws down influence for Torah study is hinted at in two Psalms connected to the Rebbe's birthday, focusing on the self-nullification in prayer that leads to the engraving of Torah.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">4)</t>
    <t s="1">Now, this matter</t>
    <t s="2">(that through prayer, [influence] is drawn down afterward also into Torah)</t>
    <t s="3">is also hinted at in the two chapters of Tehillim that pertain to the birthday</t>
    <t s="4">of the Baal HaGeulah in this year</t>
    <t s="5">(5742),</t>
    <t s="6">in Chapter 102, which they finished reciting on the eve of the birthday,</t>
    <t s="7">and in Chapter 103, which they began reciting on the birthday.</t>
    <t s="8">For in Psalm 102, it begins with the matter of prayer — "A prayer of the afflicted one," etc.,</t>
    <t s="9">and in the prayer itself — in the prayer that is at the ultimate level of self-nullification,</t>
    <t s="10">"A prayer of the afflicted when he wraps himself [in prayer] and pours out his supplication before Hashem."</t>
    <t s="11">And according to the well-known teaching of the Baal Shem Tov</t>
    <t s="12">on the verse,</t>
    <t s="13">that the prayer of the afflicted is that "before Hashem he pours out his supplication."</t>
    <t s="14">For this one, who does not request anything</t>
    <t s="15">(not even spiritual matters)</t>
    <t s="16">and all his request is to pour out his supplication before Hashem,</t>
    <t s="17">is because of the greatness of his self-nullification.</t>
    <t s="18">[And it can be said,</t>
    <t s="19">that this matter</t>
    <t s="20">(that he does not want or request anything, not even spiritual matters, and only to pour out his supplication before Hashem)</t>
    <t s="21">is</t>
    <t s="22">similar to the love of "Whom do I have in heaven? And with You I desire nothing on earth,"</t>
    <t s="23">and in the language of the Alter Rebbe:</t>
    <t s="24">"I want nothing at all; I do not want Your Gan Eden, I do not want Your World to Come, etc.; I want nothing more than You alone."</t>
    <t s="25">And it can be said,</t>
    <t s="26">that through the Alter Rebbe's saying "I want nothing more than You alone,"</t>
    <t s="27">and especially after this was publicized by the Tzemach Tzedek,</t>
    <t s="28">power was given</t>
    <t s="29">to each and every one who follows in his footsteps</t>
    <t s="30">(who holds onto the "kleamke" [handle])</t>
    <t s="31">so that in actual practice, at least, there will be something similar to this within him.</t>
    <t s="32">And especially through studying the Torah of the Alter Rebbe</t>
    <t s="33">(and certainly through studying this very matter),</t>
    <t s="34">for through this one becomes united in a wondrous unity</t>
    <t s="35">with the Torah of the Alter Rebbe,</t>
    <t s="36">and through this — with the Alter Rebbe himself].</t>
    <t s="37">And later in the Psalm,</t>
    <t s="38">it says: "This shall be written for a later generation," etc.,</t>
    <t s="39">which refers to the Torah, which is eternal.</t>
    <t s="40">And it can be said,</t>
    <t s="41">that the connection between these two matters is,</t>
    <t s="42">that the concept of the eternity of Torah in a person's service is that the Torah he studies is engraved in his mind and heart,</t>
    <t s="43">for then specifically there cannot be any change in it</t>
    <t s="44">(eternity),</t>
    <t s="45">and in order for his Torah study to be in the manner of engraving, it is through the prior service of prayer.</t>
    <t s="46">And the point of the explanation of this is,</t>
    <t s="47">that the concept of the engraving of Torah is</t>
    <t s="48">(primarily)</t>
    <t s="49">in the Torah as it is in its source,</t>
    <t s="50">in the aspect of Keter, which is above Chochmah.</t>
    <t s="51">And after it is drawn down and enclothed in Chochmah</t>
    <t s="52">[above,</t>
    <t s="53">and certainly after it descends and is enclothed in the intellect of man]</t>
    <t s="54">it is in the manner of writing.</t>
    <t s="55">And in order for Torah study with understanding and comprehension to be in the manner of engraving, it is through drawing down the source of Torah</t>
    <t s="56">(Keter)</t>
    <t s="57">into the Torah below.</t>
    <t s="58">And it can be said,</t>
    <t s="59">that this is what is written: "This shall be written for a later generation,"</t>
    <t s="60">"shall be written" is in the future tense,</t>
    <t s="61">meaning that in order for the Torah he studies to be for him in the aspect of eternity</t>
    <t s="62">("for a later generation"),</t>
    <t s="63">he must reach the level of the engraving of Torah, which is above the aspect of writing,</t>
    <t s="64">and draw down from there the aspect of the writing of Torah,</t>
    <t s="65">"shall be written" — future tense.</t>
    <t s="66">And this is the connection of "This shall be written for a later generation" to "A prayer of the afflicted," etc.,</t>
    <t s="67">that through the prior self-nullification of prayer,</t>
    <t s="68">and especially when the prayer is at the ultimate level of self-nullification,</t>
    <t s="69">that his prayer is "before Hashem he pours out his supplication,"</t>
    <t s="70">through this he draws down the revelation of Ein Sof, which is above the chain of descent,</t>
    <t s="71">and this drawing down comes afterward also into his Torah study,</t>
    <t s="72">"This shall be written for a later generation."</t>
  </section>
  <section v="7">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section discusses how Psalm 103, beginning with praise and thanksgiving, also reflects ultimate self-nullification, and how the precedence of "we will do" over "we will hear" connects this nullification to Torah study.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">5)</t>
    <t s="1">And similarly is it in Psalm 103, which begins with the matter of prayer — "Bless Hashem, O my soul,"</t>
    <t s="2">which is a prayer of praise and thanksgiving,</t>
    <t s="3">and in the prayer itself — a prayer at the ultimate level of self-nullification.</t>
    <t s="4">For the praise and thanksgiving of Dovid to the Holy One, blessed be He,</t>
    <t s="5">("Bless Hashem, O my soul")</t>
    <t s="6">was over every single occurrence,</t>
    <t s="7">as it is brought in the Gemara</t>
    <t s="8">that Dovid dwelt in five worlds and in each world he uttered song</t>
    <t s="9">(five times "Bless Hashem, O my soul"),</t>
    <t s="10">and it can be said,</t>
    <t s="11">that all the occurrences of a person are divided into five types</t>
    <t s="12">(five worlds)</t>
    <t s="13">and Dovid uttered song to the Holy One, blessed be He, over all the occurrences,</t>
    <t s="14">for uttering song to the Holy One, blessed be He, even over matters that are the opposite of apparent and revealed good, is because of the greatness and intensity of self-nullification.</t>
    <t s="15">And later in the Psalm,</t>
    <t s="16">it says: "Bless Hashem, His angels, mighty warriors who do His word, to hearken to the voice of His word,"</t>
    <t s="17">first "who do" and then "to hearken,"</t>
    <t s="18">the precedence of "we will do" over "we will hear," which was the preparation for receiving the Torah.</t>
    <t s="19">And it can be said that the connection between these two matters</t>
    <t s="20">is,</t>
    <t s="21">that the self-nullification of the precedence of "we will do" over "we will hear" is not only regarding the fulfillment of the commandments, but also in Torah study.</t>
    <t s="22">For through the fact that before the giving of the Torah they said "we will do" before "we will hear,"</t>
    <t s="23">power was given to every Jew that his Torah study should be with self-nullification,</t>
    <t s="24">in the manner of "May my tongue answer Your word,"</t>
    <t s="25">like one who answers after the one who says [it],</t>
    <t s="26">to the extent that his speech</t>
    <t s="27">(in Torah)</t>
    <t s="28">is not dependent on his will and choice,</t>
    <t s="29">to the extent that his self-nullification when he engages in Torah is comparable to the self-nullification of those above,</t>
    <t s="30">"at every single utterance their souls flew out."</t>
    <t s="31">And this is the connection of</t>
    <t s="32">("who do His word")</t>
    <t s="33">"to hearken to the voice of His word"</t>
    <t s="34">to "Bless Hashem, O my soul,"</t>
    <t s="35">for through the service of prayer,</t>
    <t s="36">and especially when the prayer is that he utters song over every occurrence</t>
    <t s="37">(five times "Bless Hashem, O my soul"),</t>
    <t s="38">the self-nullification of prayer is drawn also into his engagement with Torah.</t>
  </section>
  <section v="8">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section adds further explanation of the connection, emphasizing that the unique self-nullification in Torah study, particularly in the Oral Law which requires understanding, is drawn from the nullification expressed in the five "Bless Hashem, O my soul."</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">And one must add in explaining the connection of</t>
    <t s="1">("who do His word")</t>
    <t s="2">"to hearken to the voice of His word" to the five times "Bless Hashem, O my soul,"</t>
    <t s="3">that the primary innovation in the self-nullification of Torah study is in the Oral Torah,</t>
    <t s="4">whose study must be with understanding and comprehension</t>
    <t s="5">[for when one does not understand the explanation, it is not considered study]</t>
    <t s="6">and nevertheless the study is with self-nullification.</t>
    <t s="7">And it is similar to "at every single utterance their souls flew out,"</t>
    <t s="8">for although each utterance is a particular utterance</t>
    <t s="9">(the concept of division pertains to the understanding and comprehension of Torah)</t>
    <t s="10">nevertheless, at every single utterance their souls flew out.</t>
    <t s="11">And this is the connection of "to hearken to the voice of His word" to the five times "Bless Hashem, O my soul,"</t>
    <t s="12">for the innovation in the self-nullification of the five times "Bless Hashem, O my soul"</t>
    <t s="13">(in Psalm 103)</t>
    <t s="14">over the self-nullification of "before Hashem he pours out his supplication"</t>
    <t s="15">(in Psalm 102),</t>
    <t s="16">is,</t>
    <t s="17">that the self-nullification of "before Hashem he pours out his supplication" is that nothing matters to him</t>
    <t s="18">(for all his request is to speak with the King),</t>
    <t s="19">and the self-nullification of the five times "Bless Hashem, O my soul" that he utters song over all occurrences</t>
    <t s="20">(even over matters that are the opposite of apparent and revealed good)</t>
    <t s="21">is that even the matters that pertain to his own existence are at the ultimate level of self-nullification.</t>
    <t s="22">And through this self-nullification in prayer, it is drawn afterward also into his engagement with Torah,</t>
    <t s="23">so that even study with understanding and comprehension is with self-nullification.</t>
  </section>
</awtsmoosMeluketTranslation>
